posts.topic: A strikethrough that is a price rise
posts.why: A tactic the audience has definitely seen, named plainly.

tiktok.hook: This discount is a price rise with a strikethrough on top.
tiktok.vo: This page shows fourteen thousand crossed out and nine thousand today, except the nine was the price last month and the fourteen never existed. That is not a discount, it is a price rise with good typography. And it is a refund waiting to happen, because one person will screenshot it, and then the number you were using to seem generous becomes the number that proves you were not.
tiktok.cap: A strikethrough on a price that never existed is a lie in a font.
tiktok.body: Fourteen thousand crossed out, nine today — except nine was the price last month and fourteen never existed. That is a price rise with good typography, and it is a refund waiting to happen.

instagram.cap:
The invented original price only works until one person checks. And the people most likely to check are the ones who were going to buy.

Somebody screenshots these. Somebody always screenshots these.

facebook.body:
A page I saw shows ₦14,000 crossed out and ₦9,000 'today'.

Except ₦9,000 was the price last month, and ₦14,000 never existed.

That is not a discount. It is a price rise with good typography, and it is a refund waiting to happen — because one person will screenshot it.

Have you ever checked a crossed-out price?

posts.why: The entire offer in one sentence.

tiktok.hook: Forty five thousand separately. Thirty five together. That is it.
tiktok.vo: Forty five thousand if you buy the nine packs one at a time. Thirty five if you take them together. That is the entire offer, and there is nothing else in it. No bonus, no course, no community, no call. A bundle price, because buying nine things in one transaction is easier than buying nine things in nine transactions.
tiktok.cap: ₦45,000 separately. ₦35,000 together. That is the whole offer.
tiktok.body: Nine packs at five thousand is forty-five. All nine together is thirty-five. A bundle price, because one transaction is easier than nine. There is nothing else in the offer.

instagram.cap:
If you cannot state your offer as a single sum, it is probably two offers wearing one price tag.

One sum and one sentence. That is a complete offer.

facebook.body:
₦45,000 if you buy the nine packs one at a time.

₦35,000 if you take them together.

That is the entire offer. No bonus, no course, no community, no call.

A bundle price, because buying nine things in one transaction is easier than buying nine things in nine transactions.

Can you state your offer in one sum?

posts.why: Teaching the sum builds trust in the price.

tiktok.hook: Do the bundle maths out loud, on camera, with the actual numbers.
tiktok.vo: Do the bundle maths out loud, with the actual numbers, so anybody can check it. Nine times five is forty five. Together it is thirty five. You save ten. There is no percentage trick and no rounding, just a sum you can do on your phone in four seconds, which is exactly why it survives being checked by somebody who does not trust you yet.
tiktok.cap: 9 × ₦5,000 = ₦45,000. Together: ₦35,000. Check it on your phone.
tiktok.body: Nine times five, forty five. Together, thirty five. A sum you can do on your phone in four seconds, which is exactly why it survives being checked by someone who does not trust you yet.

instagram.cap:
Percentages invite suspicion because they hide the sum. Plain arithmetic invites a calculator, and a calculator will confirm you.

A price that survives arithmetic is a price you can defend.

facebook.body:
Do the bundle maths out loud:

Nine packs × ₦5,000 = ₦45,000.
Together: ₦35,000.
You save ₦10,000.

No percentage trick. No rounding. A sum you can do on your phone in four seconds.

That is exactly why it survives being checked by someone who does not trust you yet.

What is your sum?

posts.why: Separates a bundle from a clearance bin.

tiktok.hook: Bundle discounts work when the products are real. Otherwise, clearance.
beats: Then the bundle is a convenience
tiktok.vo: Bundle discounts work when the products are real: sold separately, at the stated price, to actual people. Otherwise it is a clearance bin with better lighting, and the customer can feel that. The test is simple. If the individual items never sell at full price, the bundle price is not a discount, it is the real price with a story attached.
tiktok.cap: If the individual items never sell at full price, the bundle is not a discount.
tiktok.body: Real products sold separately at the stated price, to actual people. If the individual items never sell at full price, the bundle price is not a discount — it is the real price with a story attached.

instagram.cap:
This is the test to apply to every bundle you are offered, including ours. Our packs sell individually at five thousand, and the arithmetic is public.

A discount from a price nobody paid is not a discount.

facebook.body:
Bundle discounts only work when the products are real: sold separately, at the stated price, to actual people.

Otherwise it is a clearance bin with better lighting, and the customer can feel that.

The test: if the individual items never sell at full price, the bundle price is not a discount. It is the real price with a story attached.

What is the last bundle you trusted?

posts.why: The customer closing themselves is the ideal sale.

tiktok.hook: She did the maths, said so I save ten, and paid.
tiktok.vo: A buyer opened her calculator while we were talking, did nine times five, looked at the bundle price and said so I save ten. Then she paid. I did not have to sell anything after that, because she had sold it to herself with arithmetic. That is what a checkable offer does: it removes the argument, and the argument is where most sales die.
tiktok.cap: She did the sum herself and said "so I save ten". Then she paid.
tiktok.body: She opened her calculator mid-conversation, did nine times five, looked at the bundle price and said so I save ten. Then she paid. The argument is where most sales die, and arithmetic removes it.

instagram.cap:
You cannot argue someone into trusting a price, but you can hand them the sum and let them decide. Most people decide faster when they can check.

The best sale is the one the customer closes with a calculator.

facebook.body:
A buyer opened her calculator while we were talking, did nine times five, looked at the bundle price and said: 'So I save ten.'

Then she paid.

I did not have to sell anything after that. She had sold it to herself with arithmetic.

That is what a checkable offer does. It removes the argument, and the argument is where most sales die.

When did a sum close something for you?

posts.topic: Name the saving, not the percentage
posts.why: A copy rule with an immediate A/B test attached.

tiktok.hook: Name the saving, not the percentage. Ten thousand beats twenty two.
tiktok.vo: Name the saving, not the percentage. Ten thousand naira beats twenty two percent, because the percentage requires a calculation and the money is already a decision. Twenty two percent could be a lot or a little depending on the price. Ten thousand is ten thousand, which is a phone, a month of transport, or the difference between a good month and a bad one.
tiktok.cap: ₦10,000 is a decision. 22% is a homework assignment.
tiktok.body: A percentage requires a calculation. The money is already a decision. Ten thousand naira is a phone, a month of transport, or the difference between a good month and a bad one.

instagram.cap:
This works in every market and every price bracket. Percentages flatter the seller; amounts help the buyer.

Say the number in the currency they actually hold.

facebook.body:
Name the saving, not the percentage.

₦10,000 beats 22% off, because the percentage needs a calculation and the money is already a decision.

22% could be a lot or a little. ₦10,000 is a phone, a month of transport, or the difference between a good month and a bad one.

Which one is on your page right now?

posts.why: A slogan-length version of the previous post.

tiktok.hook: Twenty two percent off is invisible. Ten thousand naira off is not.
tiktok.vo: Twenty two percent off is invisible, and ten thousand naira off is not, and the difference is not maths. It is that one is a proportion of something the customer has to look up, and the other is money they can already picture spending. Say the fact. Keep the percentage for the invoice.
tiktok.cap: One is a feeling. One is a fact. Say the fact.
tiktok.body: One is a proportion of something the customer has to look up. The other is money they can already picture spending. Say the fact and keep the percentage for the invoice.

instagram.cap:
The same rule applies to salaries, invoices, and your own pricing page. Amounts travel better than proportions.

Percentages are for invoices. Amounts are for people.

facebook.body:
22% off is invisible. ₦10,000 off is not.

One is a proportion of something the customer has to look up. The other is money they can already picture spending.

Say the fact. Keep the percentage for the invoice.

Which one does your page lead with?

posts.why: The answer tells you what you actually have to prove.

tiktok.hook: I asked if thirty five thousand was a lot for nine documents.
tiktok.vo: I asked whether thirty five thousand naira was a lot for nine business documents. Almost nobody answered the question directly. They all said it depends what is in them, which is the most useful thing anyone said all week, because it means the price is never the objection. The unknown is the objection. Show the inside and the price becomes a comparison instead of a number.
tiktok.cap: "It depends what is in them." The price is not the objection. The unknown is.
tiktok.body: Nobody answered the price question directly. They said it depends what is in them, which means the price is never the objection — the unknown is. Show the inside and the price becomes a comparison.

instagram.cap:
When someone says it is too expensive, they usually mean they cannot see what they are buying. Fix that first and the price conversation changes.

Price objections are usually contents objections wearing a price costume.

facebook.body:
I asked whether ₦35,000 was a lot for nine business documents.

Almost nobody answered directly. They all said it depends what is in them.

Which is the most useful thing anyone said all week, because it means the price is never the objection. The unknown is.

Show the inside and the price becomes a comparison instead of a number.

What are you leaving unknown?

tiktok.vo: The bundle saves ten thousand naira and buys you nothing new. Same thirty six files, same nine packs, one payment instead of nine. If that is worth ten thousand to you, take it. If you were only ever going to use two packs, buy two, because the bundle is a discount on volume and volume is only useful if you will use it.
tiktok.cap: Same files, ₦10,000 less, one decision. BUNDLE on WhatsApp: 0905 069 0837.
tiktok.body: Same thirty-six files, same nine packs, one payment instead of nine. If you were only going to use two packs, buy two — the bundle is a discount on volume, and volume is only useful if it gets used.

slides: Only if you will use them
instagram.cap:
This is the honest framing of every bundle ever sold: you pay less per item and you buy more items. Both halves of that sentence matter.

A discount on volume is only a discount if the volume gets used.

posts.topic: Raise prices to fake a discount
posts.why: A refusal that protects the audience from a common trick.

tiktok.hook: Asked to raise prices so a discount would look real.
beats: It is a lie with a countdown
tiktok.vo: Someone suggested we list the packs at seven thousand for a week and then announce a launch price of five, so the five looks like a favour. We said no. It would work once. Then the seven becomes the number people remember, the five becomes the real price, and every future discount has to be bigger, which is a ladder with no top. Five thousand is the price. It was five thousand last month.
tiktok.cap: The price was ₦5,000 last month. It is ₦5,000 this month. That is the discount.
tiktok.body: List at seven, announce five, and the five looks like a favour. It works once. Then the seven is what people remember and every future discount has to be bigger, which is a ladder with no top.

instagram.cap:
Every invented discount raises the number the customer expects to pay later. It is borrowing attention now and repaying it every month after.

Fake urgency is a loan against your next price.

facebook.body:
Someone suggested we list the packs at ₦7,000 for a week, then announce a launch price of ₦5,000 so the five looks like a favour.

We said no.

It would work once. Then ₦7,000 becomes the number people remember, ₦5,000 becomes the real price, and every future discount has to be bigger. A ladder with no top.

₦5,000 is the price. It was ₦5,000 last month.

posts.why: Gives the buyer a defence against every discount in their feed.

tiktok.hook: Before you compare two offers, compare the unit price. Every time.
beats: Divide by the number of things
tiktok.vo: Before you compare two offers, compare the unit price. Divide the total by the number of things you actually get, per file, per month, per session. A bundle that looks cheaper per item is only cheaper if you use the items, so the real unit is not the file, it is the file you open. That single division has saved me more money than any advice I have ever read.
tiktok.cap: Divide by what you will use, not by what is in the box.
tiktok.body: Divide the total by the number of things you will actually use. A bundle that looks cheaper per item is only cheaper if the items get opened.

instagram.cap:
This works for data bundles, subscriptions, courses and gym memberships. The maths is always the same and it is always unflattering to the bigger package.

The real unit is the thing you open, not the thing you bought.

facebook.body:
Before you compare two offers, compare the unit price.

Divide the total by the number of things you actually get — per file, per month, per session.

Then divide it again by the number you will actually use.

A bundle that looks cheaper per item is only cheaper if the items get opened.

The real unit is the file you open, not the file you bought.
